speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see a pattern of recurrent joint swelling and pain that doesn't fit a simple injury. To start, does the pain in your right knee feel better when you rest it, or does it improve with movement and activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and previous ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), recent sexual activity, and a family history of autoimmune conditions strongly suggests this diagnosis. I will request images of the right knee and a urine analysis to confirm inflammation and rule out other causes.
